review: Hokum is an atmospheric horror/mystery with a great, fail-proof setting - an old haunted hotel around Halloween. This is the third horror/mystery by the director of Caveat and Oddity, and I feel both of those films are superior to Hokum. Part of the problem is how unlikable the main character is. Much like in The Shining and 1408, he’s a troubled writer who drinks and must confront his past and his demons at the hotel. But the mystery of what happens to the missing girl isn’t all that mysterious, and has little or nothing to do with him. Great movies stay with you and leave you thinking about the meaning or how they end. After Hokum I could barely remember how it ended or why the hotel was haunted at all. Maybe I need a second viewing. But both Caveat and Oddity had a more focused story, with better characters.
